sections.label: A
sections.title: Circle the correct answer.
sections.note: Choose True or False for each science statement.

questions.prompt: 1. A sailboat uses wind to move across the water.
questions.explanation: A sailboat can use wind energy to move across the water, so the statement is true.

questions.prompt: 2. Pollution is good for the Earth.
questions.explanation: Pollution harms the environment, so the statement is false.

questions.prompt: 3. Coal is a type of food.
questions.explanation: Coal is a non-renewable fossil fuel, not a type of food.

sections.label: B
sections.title: Look and complete the sentences.
sections.note: Use each clean source picture to identify the energy word.

questions.prompt: 1. A ___ is a source of energy.
questions.explanation: The picture shows a wind turbine. A wind farm is a group of wind turbines, so the official key accepts either expression here.

questions.prompt: 2. We use ___ to heat our homes.
questions.explanation: The picture shows oil beside a container. Oil can be burned to heat homes.

questions.prompt: 3. A ___ burns fossil fuels to create energy.
questions.explanation: The picture shows a power plant, where fossil fuels can be burned to produce energy.

questions.prompt: 4. The burners of our stove use ___.
questions.explanation: The picture shows a gas stove burner. The full vocabulary term is natural gas.

sections.label: C
sections.title: Unscramble the words and match.
sections.note: Write the word, then choose its definition label. The letters a-c are labels only.
wordBank: a. an energy source with many turbines
c. light bulbs, TVs, and computers need this to work

questions.prompt: 1. y c i t l e e i t c r

parts.label: Definition label
parts.explanation: Light bulbs, TVs, and computers need electricity, so the definition label is c.

questions.prompt: 2. o n n - n e r e a w l e b

parts.label: Definition label
parts.explanation: A non-renewable resource cannot be used again after it is exhausted, so the label is b.

questions.prompt: 3. d i w n  a r m f

parts.label: Unscrambled word
parts.explanation: Wind farm is the standard spelling.

parts.label: Definition label
parts.explanation: A wind farm is an energy source made up of many turbines, so the label is a.

sections.label: D
sections.title: Listen. Then circle the correct answer.
sections.note: Listen for whether each possibility is positive or negative.

options: He might like to see a wind farm.
He might not like to see a wind farm.
answers: He might like to see a wind farm.
questions.explanation: The recording says he might like to see a wind farm.

options: It might be a power plant.
It might not be a power plant.
answers: It might be a power plant.
questions.explanation: The recording presents a possible identification: it might be a power plant.

options: The wind turbines might not work.
answers: The wind turbines might not work.
questions.explanation: The recording uses the negative possibility might not work.
The recording says it might cause pollution.

sections.label: E
sections.title: Complete the sentences.
sections.note: Choose from the box to complete the sentences. There is one extra word or phrase.

questions.prompt: 1. This town ___ a power plant, but I'm not sure.
questions.explanation: I'm not sure signals possibility, so might have fits the sentence.

questions.prompt: 2. It's windy today. It ___ for sailing.
questions.explanation: Wind can make the day suitable for sailing, but it is only a possibility.

questions.prompt: 3. How much do solar panels cost? I think they ___.
questions.explanation: I think shows uncertainty, so may be very expensive is appropriate.

questions.prompt: 4. This camera is very old. You can try it, but it ___.
questions.explanation: Because the camera is very old, there is a possibility that it will not work.

sections.label: F
sections.title: Look and complete the sentences with may, might, may not, or might not and a verb.
sections.note: Use the evidence in each picture to express a possibility.

questions.prompt: 1. She ___ money.
questions.explanation: Her empty wallet suggests that she may not have any money.

questions.prompt: 2. The car ___ gas.
questions.explanation: The driver appears worried and the car may not have gas.

questions.prompt: 3. They ___ to a wind farm.
questions.explanation: The children are near wind turbines, so they might go to a wind farm.

questions.prompt: 4. It ___ sunny today.
questions.explanation: The sun in the picture suggests that it might be sunny today.

sections.label: G
sections.title: Two of the three words are incorrect. Listen and circle the correct answer.
sections.note: Choose the one word from each row that matches the recording.

questions.explanation: The word in the recording is traffic jam.

sections.label: H
sections.title: Match the sentences to the pictures.
sections.note: The letters a-d label the pictures only. Choose the picture that matches each sentence.

questions.prompt: 1. Let's take the elevator to the fourth floor.
questions.explanation: Picture b shows a person inside an elevator.

questions.prompt: 2. The ambulance will take us quickly to the hospital.
questions.explanation: Picture d shows an ambulance.

questions.prompt: 3. I hear a fire engine. There must be a fire nearby.
questions.explanation: Picture a shows a fire engine.

questions.prompt: 4. Sometimes Arthur takes a carpool to work.
questions.explanation: Picture c shows several passengers sharing one car, which is a carpool.

sections.label: I
sections.title: Complete the sentences.
sections.note: Write the transportation or city word that completes each meaning.

questions.prompt: 1. I called a ___ to take us to the movie. It should be here in ten minutes.
questions.explanation: A taxi is a car that you call to take you somewhere.

questions.prompt: 2. A ___ can fly over all the cars in a traffic jam.
questions.explanation: A helicopter travels through the air, so it can fly over a traffic jam.

questions.prompt: 3. The ___ is a train that goes under the city.
questions.explanation: A subway is an underground city train.

questions.prompt: 4. I lost a ___ on my shirt. I need to sew on a new one tonight.
questions.explanation: A button can be sewn onto a shirt.

sections.label: J
sections.title: Circle the correct answer.
sections.note: Use the context to choose a few, a little, or a lot of.

questions.prompt: 1. There are ___ taxis. You can find one easily.
questions.explanation: If a taxi is easy to find, there are a lot of taxis.

questions.prompt: 2. We have only ___ gas. We need to get more soon.
questions.explanation: Only and the need to get more show that the amount of gas is small.

questions.prompt: 3. The library has ___ books about energy and pollution. I won't have a problem finding one.
questions.explanation: If finding a book is not a problem, the library has a lot of books on the topic.

sections.label: K
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order to make sentences.
sections.note: Use every word and add correct punctuation.

questions.prompt: 1. Ed / a lot / of / has / paper
answers: Ed has a lot of paper
Ed has a lot of paper.
questions.explanation: Place the subject first, followed by has and the quantity phrase a lot of paper.

questions.prompt: 2. We / a few / apples / eat / every day
answers: We eat a few apples every day
We eat a few apples every day.
questions.explanation: Use subject + verb + quantity phrase + time expression.

questions.prompt: 3. games / The students / of / play / a lot
answers: The students play a lot of games
The students play a lot of games.
questions.explanation: A lot of comes directly before the plural count noun games.

questions.prompt: 4. energy / uses / The computer / a little
answers: The computer uses a little energy
The computer uses a little energy.
questions.explanation: A little comes before the uncountable noun energy.

sections.label: L
sections.title: Write the words in the correct order to make questions. Then match them to the pictures.
sections.note: Write the complete question, then choose its picture label. The letters a-c are labels only.

questions.prompt: 1. a / lot / of / books / Does / she / have

parts.label: Picture label
parts.explanation: Picture b shows a woman with a lot of books.

parts.label: Complete question
answers: Does she have a lot of books
Does she have a lot of books?
parts.explanation: A present simple question with she uses Does + subject + base verb.

questions.prompt: 2. make / a / lot / pollution / Does / the factory / of

parts.label: Picture label
parts.explanation: Picture c shows pollution from a factory.

parts.label: Complete question
answers: Does the factory make a lot of pollution
Does the factory make a lot of pollution?
parts.explanation: Use Does + the factory + make + a lot of pollution.

questions.prompt: 3. questions / have / a / Do / the students / few

parts.label: Picture label
parts.explanation: Picture a shows students raising their hands to ask questions.

parts.label: Complete question
answers: Do the students have a few questions
Do the students have a few questions?
parts.explanation: A present simple question with the plural subject students uses Do.
